family_assessments.assessment: Intended to reconstruct one trustee handover at the bank-meeting cut-off despite signature cues and later administration. The blind review verifies that a registered release effects simultaneous retirement and replacement and that an affirmative hold preserves the incumbent (family_a/review/blind-review.md). Fresh excerpt and necessity checks establish the instrument-plus-disposition route and reject the proposed short route (family_a/review/necessity.md). A0/A1 reorder the same Sources without changing the key or ordinary context; A0/A2 change the disposition (family_a/review/matched-sources.json). The bank and diary material adds a supported kinship and non-operative cues. Frequency and the later note favour the incumbent; draft promotion favours the successor. A two-person office and explanatory wording limit the inference beyond this case.
family_assessments.overlap: Shares joint proof with B and C. Unlike D, it changes whether an act took effect, not which provision an effective act reaches. Retain the release and order controls; do not treat the bank material as an independent administrative-context test.

family_assessments.assessment: Intended to resolve the speaker of a parentage report through an independently maintained attendance field. In B0/B1 only the name field changes: the completed record binds the native statement to one speaker, while the incomplete record leaves two compatible speakers and preserves the ordinary parent edge (family_b/review/outputs/comparison.json; family_b/review/agreement.json). The relay and export share one informant; forward-only readings do not identify the speaker, and deletion of a needed statement or identity fact defeats the target (family_b/review/mask-results.json; family_b/review/proof-deletions.json). The independent original-document sighting adds ordinary kinship. A field-completeness check followed by first-contact selection can reproduce the edge delta under this two-name desk convention.
family_assessments.overlap: Like C, it withholds a named edge when the identifier is incomplete, but the link identifies a statement's speaker rather than a trust. Unlike F, the discriminating identity information really is missing. Retain it as a bounded attribution and shared-origin case.

family_assessments.assessment: Intended to allocate an operative designation between two trusts through a separately maintained parent-deed reference. The matched reference changes the supported trust endpoint, and the partial reference leaves both allocations viable and neither endpoint licensed (family_c/review/outputs/comparison.json; family_c/review/agreement.json). Fresh excerpt review verifies the three-Source proof; whole-file masks defeat the target and preserve ten ordinary edges (family_c/review/proof-deletions.json). Shared trustees, routine meeting, wish and expense material add context but are not separate interventions. First-trust, fixed-trust and assign-both rules fail across the variants, but a single register entry and two parallel settlements bound the join.
family_assessments.overlap: Extends A/B joint-proof exposure to an operative trust endpoint and supplies the strongest admitted invariant-graph check. It does not isolate distraction, graph size or the effect of document volume.

family_assessments.assessment: Intended to isolate the reach of an effective amendment. The admitted D0/D1 control changes only the provision locator: the earlier survivor changes, while the replacement and unaffected trust relationships persist. The saved keys attach joint scope proof to each current beneficiary, and the closing audit independently verifies the grouped proof. The principal extract contains separate office and beneficiary provisions; the variation's effective date stays fixed. The locator alone can reproduce the graph, individual fact-level deletion coverage remains incomplete, and unrelated kinship was outside the comparison. Retain the scoped-amendment finding without generalising to other mechanisms of amendment.
family_assessments.overlap: Complements A by fixing effectiveness. It tests a scope change that changes the roster; it does not test whether two separately operative provisions can sustain one identical scored edge while the valid proof changes.

family_assessments.assessment: Intended to test a populated display-label collision without removing identity evidence. The F0/F1 control preserves the complete named graph and the separately attached proof sets after changing a single ancillary label. The masked review defeats a dependent edge when the exact identity entry is withheld. Stable references and the explicit reconciliation are authoritative; the working index is not. Positional pairing still reproduces the graph. The original isolated reader explained the correct identity but entered a different structured surname; the independent repeat on the identical packet returned the correct surname. Retain the collision result and the distinction between explanation and exact structured recovery.
family_assessments.overlap: Complements B's genuinely incomplete speaker field and C's partial trust reference. It does not cover duplicate authoritative identities, identity interacting with other missing facts, or general collision robustness.

gaps.finding: A, B and C verify dependent positive routes; D verifies grouped scope proof; F checks exact identity attachment under graph invariance. D still lacks full fact-level deletion coverage. AD already reserves alternative evidence for the same relationship. The distinct gap is a change in which substantive provision itself licenses an invariant edge, such that a formerly valid attachment becomes insufficient.

Release, selective amendment and documentary scope have separate exposure. Outstanding questions include distinguishing a named representative from the actual officeholder when the latter cannot be represented in the graph, and identifying which date governs a person's authority to make a decision whose effect is deferred. Neither requires new scoring predicates.

B verifies one origin and its relay, not competing independent origins. The earlier E comparison was returned on documentary realism, and the newly qualified E and W revisions are not yet admitted. Review those before commissioning more disagreement cases; do not use the earlier E comparison as admitted coverage.

B, C and F give repeated but bounded identity and withholding checks. Broader collisions and interacting gaps lack a clean diagnostic control; exact names that are not distinguishable under the current contract should not be forced into a fixture. AB's non-entailment from common parentage, AG's exhaustive negative coverage and AH's field-limited attestation are separate reserved mechanisms, not invitations to duplicate them.

C's ordinary edges are an invariant-graph check and A's order-only sibling holds the actual text and chronology fixed. X's qualification addresses the presence of support in a routine reply. None establishes a burial, placement or volume effect. Any such claim would require a dedicated fixed-truth control and intact whole-file review; intermediate capacity does not establish large-tier capacity.

T tests inspection scope within the supplied file and J reserves authentication linked to delivery; neither authorises external retrieval. A missing record can leave a graph claim unresolved, but acquiring it, recovering physical text or asking a practitioner to settle the matter would extend the study boundary. Do not infer an interaction from a jointly necessary proof or from review masks.

result.portfolio_summary: The admitted portfolio contains five independent Matter histories: A, B, C, D and F. Count each matched family once. Repeated exposure is strongest for cross-Source proof, documentary authority and evidence sufficiency; the recurring completeness check is preservation of unaffected edges. The primary interventions nevertheless differ: release, speaker attribution, trust allocation, amendment scope and a display-label collision. A alone supplies an order-only sibling. The most useful remaining question is not simply whether another file requires a join, but whether that join tests a different decision and exposes a different failure in the graph or its attached evidence. X and T are technically qualified, not admitted: X supplies a matched incidental-assertion contrast in native correspondence, not a placement or workload effect; T supplies an intermediate, intact-file inspection-scope case, not a matched custody or volume effect. The packet also reports newly qualified N revision 3, E revision 3 and W revision 2. None is counted as admitted, and E's historical return applies to the earlier reviewed material, not as a verdict on revision 3. Rank the reserve AP first for an invariant graph with a controlled change in sufficient proof, AQ second for a lower-cost check on attribution to the wrong kind of actor, and AR third for authority at the time of exercise rather than at the reporting cut-off. These are three proposals, not approvals or commitments. The ten-family planning target and the 19-history pre-giant technical goal are different milestones; neither warrants padding the reserve. The intermediate and large workloads remain separate commitments. No paid extraction results or sealed evaluation material support claims about model difficulty, practitioner performance or prevalence.

evidence_dependencies: Two isolated readers per condition derive complete keys. Fresh readers test exact excerpts for separate operative bases, the selected locator and effective substitution, and the unchanged review time. Test singletons and all plausible shorter or alternative routes before deciding which passages are necessary.

Remove the surviving provision's necessary named assertion, the trust or provision linkage, and the operative scope fact separately, including copies of a removed fact. Separately mask the displaced schedule and the variation. Rederive each complete diagnostic key: masking the variation can restore an original route rather than merely delete support. Verify exact evidence excluding the displaced basis without scoring a negative relationship.

Audit both directions from edge to passages and from apparent assertions to the key. Credit any genuinely sufficient subset, but return the design if one unchanged short route sustains the earlier edge in both conditions.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The earlier and replacement named beneficiary edges each appear once in both keys. For the earlier edge the sufficient attachment must reach a basis still operative in that condition; merely quoting the named row from the displaced provision is insufficient. Report graph recovery separately from proof recovery.
genres_and_provenance: A verified principal instrument extract from the trustees' retained operative file identifies the trust, the separable authority to vary a provision and an unaffected relationship.
Two signed standing schedules, each issued and retained for a different benefit purpose, record the separately usable named provisions.
An executed variation retained in the trustees' decision file refers to the affected schedule by its ordinary locator and supplies the substitution and effective date.
The trust accountant's prior-period reconciliation, retained with the supporting accounts, documents payments under the earlier arrangements.
A trustee minute retained in the governance file commissions advice before the next payments without resolving the current named roster.
The adviser's dated brief retained on the review file fixes the cut-off and distinguishes the roster question from payment reconciliation.
design.intervention: Change exactly one literal provision locator in the effective variation. Both locators are valid under the unchanged instrument. Hold every other Source byte and the presentation order fixed.
invariants: The complete exact-name graph, effective date, replacement wording, trust, people, prior payments and cut-off stay fixed.
The independently supported office and its sufficient proof stay fixed. The named substitute is licensed in both conditions, with scope checked separately in each.
negative_controls: Historic payment is not a surviving provision and cannot rescue a displaced proof.
Loss of one basis is not denial of the beneficiary relationship. An unrelated trust role remains supported after target-only diagnostics.
design.scenario: The adviser compares two continuing benefit purposes with a limited substitution and historic disbursements. The graph projects both purposes onto one relationship per person and trust, but the briefing must not treat the displaced basis as current.
shortcut_heuristics: Test latest-instrument-only, remove-the-person, union-of-provisions and cite-both rules. An unchanged graph alone cannot demonstrate recovery of scope.
Inspect headings, filenames, quoted rows, order and accounting labels for a leaked survivor or a self-sufficient current roster. Reordering is review-only.
success_criteria: Independent complete graphs agree across the pair and the exact-byte comparison verifies the sole permitted edit. Fresh readers confirm the non-interchangeable current proof routes and the diagnostic keys without consulting a proposed key.

Stop if the two purposes create different trusts, either locator is unnatural, a normally retained roster bypasses the switch, or the comparison requires an amended scorer or an outside legal conclusion.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and integration 10–15; blind full-file and fresh proof review 10–16; adjudication and bidirectional audit 7–11; owner review 2–4. Assumes two isolated readers per branch and at most one pre-lock documentary revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 7 natural Sources. Two independently retained schedules are warranted only if both serve real administrative purposes. Plan four full-file recoveries and a fresh proof pass per branch, followed by targeted scope, linkage, surviving-row and variation diagnostics.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse D's exact-byte and amendment-scope checks, C's complete-graph and diagnostic-key checks, and existing same-edge sufficient-subset scoring.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use beneficiary_of and existing invariant trust predicates. Provisions and payment purposes are evidence or briefing context, not nodes or parallel edges. No negative predicate is needed.
risks_and_limits: The primary comparison demonstrates whether the attachment follows scope on this file, not the difficulty or prevalence of parallel provisions.
Do not force citations to every document or count any review mask as a benchmark condition.

assumptions: The principal terms expressly permit selective replacement. Each provision by itself can establish the same named beneficiary relationship with the trust, and neither controls or depends on the other.

The same variation wording could naturally apply to either provision. Prior accounts close before the variation takes effect, and no fixed minute, payment instruction or later consolidated schedule settles which provision was selected.
grounding.documentary_situation: Two independently usable provisions of the same trust serve different purposes and name the same person. A limited variation substitutes another named person in exactly one provision. The provisions are separately documented for their actual administration, not separate trusts.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile a limited variation against separate standing benefit provisions and the prior accounting period before advising on the next payments.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Report current named beneficiary relationships and identify the provision that still supplies each relationship, separately from the payment history.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether both provisions would ordinarily be kept in separately issued schedules and brought together for this review.
Whether both locator alternatives fit the same decision wording and retained chronology without suppressing a naturally available controlling record.

references.relevance: Supports retaining instruments, decisions, payment records and minutes. The fictional file must establish the effect and separability of the two provisions.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Trust administration advice on which named provisions remain available after a selective variation under express terms of one trust.

objective.coverage_gap: D changes the earlier survivor at graph level; it cannot expose a proof error masked by an invariant edge sustained through a different operative basis. AD removes alternative evidence for one fact in review; it does not make the underlying provision inapplicable while the other provision remains in force.
objective.failure_mechanism: The renderer may remove the earlier beneficiary altogether, duplicate the relationship by provision, or produce the right graph while citing the provision that no longer supports it.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: Switching the selected provision leaves the complete named graph invariant but switches which original provision can support the earlier beneficiary's current edge. An exact graph with a sufficient attachment in each condition disconfirms the predicted errors for this file.

proposals.title: One beneficiary edge, a different surviving provision

evidence_dependencies: Two isolated full-file readers reconstruct the exact graph and separately describe both capacities. Fresh readers verify exact passages for the personal office and representative signature and test the strongest singleton, including any mandate passage that actually attests office rather than labelling a signature.

Test the office and capacity components independently, removing copies of deleted facts. Rederive complete diagnostic graphs and record positive evidence of representation and why it does not support personal office. If another sufficient route exists, credit it; do not require a delegation citation on an independently established personal office edge.
Audit every apparent office label, copied acknowledgement and signature block against the exact actor and capacity it describes.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The individual office edge survives removal of provider administration when independently proved. A representative whose personal office is not established remains unscored. If removing a capacity passage leaves representation open, register that as uncertainty rather than reclassifying the signer.
genres_and_provenance: A verified current operative extract supplied from retained trust papers identifies the trust, the officeholders and an unrelated supported relationship.
A dated corporate delegation record retained by the corporate trustee and supplied with the mandate documentation identifies its representative and the scope of that person's authority.
An executed provider mandate retained by the investment provider and on the handover file records the account instructions and both signature capacities.
The provider's native implementation acknowledgement, retained by the adviser, shows what instructions were received and processed without independently confirming personal offices.
A dated holdings statement from the provider, retained in the administration papers, identifies the holdings to which the handover relates without conferring a relationship.
A dated adviser brief retained on the handover file sets the review scope and cut-off without restating the office roster.
design.intervention: Score one intact natural file. For review only, separately mask the provider paperwork and remove the independently operative personal-office assertion with its copies. Separately test deletion of the capacity wording and rederive what can still be concluded about the signatory; do not manufacture another mandate.
invariants: The authorised signer, individual co-trustee, principal, account and review date remain fixed in the full file.
The unrelated graph and its sufficient evidence are independent of mandate processing.
negative_controls: The company's case-specific representative and the officeholder's own signature are not equivalent merely because both appear on one mandate.
An unrelated named relationship remains recoverable; mandate and holdings records must not turn into a source of additional trustee relationships.
design.scenario: An adviser reviews one investment mandate on which both signatures are needed for the practical handover. One is an act of a named individual officeholder; the other is expressly representative. The adviser must preserve the positive personal office without promoting the delegate.
shortcut_heuristics: Check nearest-human attribution, role-label matching, emission of all signers and suppression of all signers.
Check that filenames, wrappers, Source order and the brief do not name the answer. A signature capacity is substantive evidence, not metadata to strip.
success_criteria: Independent readers agree on the full graph and on the exact positive and presumptively misleading passages, and fresh checks establish which subsets are sufficient. The full file, not the masks, is the only scored condition.

Stop if corporate law must be supplied from outside, if the two signature roles are not ordinarily retained and distinguishable, or if the case requires scoring an organisation or a representation edge.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring 7–11; blind and fresh excerpt or mask review 7–11; adjudication and audit 5–8; owner review 2–3. Assumes one provider workflow, no speculative office dispute and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 6 natural Sources. Plan two full-file recoveries, one focused exact-passage check of each signing capacity and three targeted office, representation and provider-paper diagnostics.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse A's office-proof checks, F's wrong-person attachment audit and the existing complete-graph and exact-passage checks.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Score the explicitly supported personal trustee_of edge and other licensed Person/Trust relationships. The corporate trustee, its signatory authority and open capacity questions are described in the companion register, not represented by new nodes or predicates.
risks_and_limits: A well-labelled mandate may be easy. This is a check on correct actor and capacity attribution, not an estimate of difficulty or an effect of signature layout.
This natural-only case cannot identify a causal effect of adding corporate representation or characterise how providers ordinarily verify mandates.

assumptions: The retained office record and representation record explicitly distinguish the two signing capacities. No inference about the legal validity of the signature or appointment is required.
Provider receipt and processing of the mandate are genuinely necessary to the handover but do not create personal office. No person is used as a substitute node for the company.
grounding.documentary_situation: The supplied current office record names a corporate trustee and an individual co-trustee. The same transaction mandate carries signatures by the individual in their own trustee capacity and by a different named individual solely for the corporate trustee.
grounding.legal_workflow: Review a trust investment-provider mandate and the corresponding office records before completing an account administration handover.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Produce the Person/Trust relationship briefing and list representative and account authorities separately.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether the provider would naturally retain a single mandate with separately stated capacities and whether the adviser would receive it with the current office and delegation records.
Whether the effective operative roster is ordinarily confirmable from the proposed retained extract at that stage.

references.relevance: Grounds retention of investment information and trustee decisions, not a provider's mandate format or any rule of corporate representation.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Advise on who holds trust office and who is documented as acting for an officeholder in the mandate process.

objective.coverage_gap: O tests whether a title application changes an independently fixed office; it does not test projection of an actual office from an unscored principal to a human who signs for it. S tests two possible relationships of the same person, not two different actors behind superficially similar signatures.
objective.failure_mechanism: The renderer may assign the corporate office to the nearest named human, emit an out-of-contract corporate node, or avoid both errors by suppressing the individual co-trustee. The briefing may describe documented representation as personal office even if the graph is correct.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: A natural mandate pack permits exact recovery of the independently established individual trustee and other supported relationships without attributing the company's office to its representative. Exact recovery, sufficient attachment and correct treatment of the two signatures disconfirm those errors on this file.

proposals.title: A named signatory is not necessarily a named trustee

evidence_dependencies: Two isolated readers independently reconstruct the complete file and identify the exact passages for exercise-time authority, the transition, deferred effect and cut-off. Fresh readers test the needed proof subsets for the beneficiary and current office separately, including whether the succession instrument also establishes prior authority.

Delete necessary components one at a time with their copies. Independently rederive each diagnostic key, including any fallback under the retained terms. Verify the exact evidence for the maker's exclusion from current office without emitting a negative edge.

Audit against a short route from the signed designation, a later summary or a purported ratification. Accept ordinary corroborating routes when sufficient, but return the design if checking the historical capacity or express timing rule is dispensable.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The full file supports the designated beneficiary and the current officeholder, not a current trustee edge for the outgoing maker. Missing evidence of a necessary date or rule leaves the affected claim unresolved unless a verified alternative route remains. A transition mask may change the recoverable roster, so do not assume masks only subtract edges.
genres_and_provenance: A verified principal extract retained by the trustees supplies the power, the exercise-time authority rule, the express continuation rule and an unaffected provision.
The outgoing trustee's retained appointment instrument documents the basis and start of office before the decision.
The dated signed designation in the trustee decision file records the maker, the named beneficiary and the fixed later effective date.
The executed retirement and succession instrument, retained with the governance records, supplies the intervening change of office.
A dated native query retained from the trust accountant seeks instructions for the next period without pronouncing on office or entitlement.
The adviser's dated review brief retained on the advice file states the cut-off and the purpose of the briefing.
design.intervention: Score one natural file with the complete chronology. Use review-only separate deletions of the exercise-time authority rule, the evidence that the maker held office at exercise, and the deferred-effect or continuation fact. Mask the transition record separately and independently reconstruct the resulting graph. Do not create a sibling in which a formerly authorised actor inexplicably signs after retirement.
invariants: The natural sequence of exercise, handover, effect and review is fixed, as are the exact people, trust and unrelated provision.
The current office proof is checked independently of whether the designation's deferred effect is established.
negative_controls: Neither the accountant's request nor the successor's administrative work proves an exercise of the power.
The unrelated provision survives target-only removals. A valid pre-handover decision does not establish that its maker still holds office.
design.scenario: The next payment review falls after both the handover and the scheduled start of a named provision. Earlier appointment papers and the handover evidence are needed to assess the maker's dated authority and the separate current trustee roster.
shortcut_heuristics: Test evaluate-all-at-cut-off, evaluate-authority-at-effect, latest-officeholder-as-maker and signature-alone rules.
Check dates, captions, ordering, summaries and independently repeated office dates for an answer cue or shorter proof. Natural dates may locate the acts; they do not supply the authority rule.
success_criteria: Whole-file readers agree on exact edges and independent excerpt and removal reviewers agree on the role of each relevant time. The graph and the same-edge proof must both pass.
Stop if a later confirmation would normally be indispensable, the apparent survival depends on outside law, or no natural pack makes the historically relevant authority separately testable.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and chronology integration 9–14; blind whole-file and fresh excerpt or mask review 9–14; adjudication and audit 6–10; owner review 2–4. Assumes a single transition, fixed express rules and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 6 natural Sources. Plan two complete file recoveries, an independent typed-chronology check and targeted diagnostics for the rule, historical capacity, deferred effect and transition.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse A's office and cut-off audit, D's rederived fallback checks and the dated-event distinctions planned in R.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use trustee_of, beneficiary_of and existing invariant relationships. Authority at exercise, past office, event dates and deferred effect belong in evidence or the companion register rather than as new scored assertions.
risks_and_limits: One natural chronology does not estimate a causal time-of-authority effect. The diagnostics verify the proof requirements only.
Defer if ordinary recordkeeping would collapse the office history and operative facts into a single conclusive record and eliminate the intended dependency.

assumptions: The fictional terms expressly test authority when the decision is made, preserve a properly made deferred decision through a change of office and require no later approval.

The next accounting decision gives all records an ordinary reason to be reviewed together. The outgoing decision, retirement and succession, effective date and review are distinct, with no unrecorded gap that needs adjudication.
grounding.documentary_situation: A decision is made while its maker holds the required office. A separate handover then ends that office, and the decision takes effect on its previously fixed date before the review. The new officeholder does not make or ratify the decision.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile an outgoing officer's retained decision with the documented office handover before a scheduled disbursement review.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Distinguish decision date, office transition, effective date and review cut-off before advising on prospective payments.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether an ordinary delayed-effect decision and independently dated office papers would be retained together without a controlling implementation minute that also attests earlier authority.
Whether the supplied texts would clearly distinguish prior authority from current office without contrived restatement.

references.relevance: Supports keeping trust decisions, deeds of appointment and payment records; it does not establish when authority is tested or whether an act survives a change of office.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Advise on the current beneficiary relationship and current trustee roster when a pre-handover act is expressed to take effect later.

objective.coverage_gap: R distinguishes a triggering event date from a later report date; it does not require checking the actor's capacity at a different date from the act's effect. A switches the occurrence of release itself. AC switches the duration of the provision. AR fixes the effect and tests which point in the office history establishes authority.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may test the maker's eligibility at the effective date or the cut-off, treat the current trustee as the maker, or carry a former office forward to justify a valid decision.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: Independent reconstruction can license the designated beneficiary through the maker's authority at exercise and the deferred effect, while excluding the maker from the current trustee roster. Exact graph and sufficient proof recovery disconfirm the predicted errors on the natural file.

proposals.title: A decision survives the end of its maker's office

stopping_criteria: Before authoring, justify each Source by participant, real business purpose, custody and availability by the cut-off. Reject contradictory fixed chronology, missing normally controlling records, artificial splitting and padding. Use supplied public references for documented genres and workflows only; mark file-specific practices as provisional.

Before any technical qualification, require isolated complete reconstruction of every scored condition, exact passage attribution for positive support and for exclusions, and independent rederivation of the diagnostic keys. Verify sufficient subsets and separately remove genuinely necessary components with their copies. A correct graph with insufficient or misattached proof is not a proof pass.

Return a matched design if more than the predeclared literal changes, if another sufficient route defeats the intended contrast, or if cues in wrappers, order or filenames substitute for the claimed proof. For natural-only files, keep masks unscored and report no causal comparison.

Defer if the result needs a new node type or predicate, external retrieval, OCR, an outside legal determination, inaccessible or held-out material, or a stitched section key in place of independent intact-file review. Keep open propositions separate from negative findings and from scored edges.

Keep this a reserve. Recheck marginal value against separately admitted revisions before activating a design. Stop once the distinct, credible and reviewable proposals are exhausted, regardless of the family-count target; technical qualification is not human admission.
